guideTitle: Best Large Wall Clocks for the Living Room (2026)
metaTitle: Best Large Wall Clocks for Living Rooms (2026)
metaDescription: Seven large silent wall clocks compared on diameter, movement, readability, frame material and hanging weight, with honest tradeoffs for real living rooms.
expertTake: The CLXEAST 24 inch matte black clock is the best overall pick for its thick metal build and clear Roman numerals, while the Westclox 20 inch is the value pick for smaller walls. The EMAX HOME 30 inch suits buyers who want a rustic oversized statement. Anyone who needs to check the time from across a large open room at night should skip decorative clocks and buy a lighted or digital one.
introParagraphs: A large wall clock is both a timekeeper and a piece of wall art, and the right size and style can anchor a sofa wall or fill an awkward blank space. The wrong one is too small to read, too loud to sleep near or too heavy for the wall hanger.

The decisions that matter are diameter, numeral style, movement type and frame weight. This guide compares seven battery-operated clocks, mostly silent quartz, on readability and build so you can pick one that looks right and keeps good time.

products.name: CLXEAST 24 Inch Silent Matte Black Metal Wall Clock with Roman Numerals
products.description:
CLXEAST makes a 24 inch matte black metal clock with a frame that is 0.8 inches thick, which gives it more shadow depth and visual weight than a thin ring. The movement is described as a non-ticking quartz mechanism, and the clock hangs from a round keyhole mount. Roman numerals give a classic look that suits industrial and traditional rooms.

Roman numerals are elegant but slower to read at a glance than Arabic numerals, especially for children. The tradeoff is that a 24 inch dial is medium sized, so it works best on a wall with some breathing room, not a very large open wall. Compared with the SwallowLiving, the CLXEAST has a heavier frame and a cleaner matte finish, while the SwallowLiving has a white face with bold black numerals.

Hang it on a stud or a rated anchor at eye level, with the center around 57 to 60 inches from the floor. Insert a fresh AA battery, set the time and test the silent sweep. Dust the frame with a dry cloth, and wipe the glass lightly. Replace the battery yearly. It suits a living room, a dining room or an office with a modern industrial feel.
products.bestFor: Living rooms and offices that want a silent, heavy-framed clock with a classic dial.
pros: A 0.8 inch thick metal frame gives real depth and visual weight
A silent non-ticking movement suits bedrooms and living rooms
Matte black finish resists glare and fingerprints
A 24 inch diameter fits most sofa and console walls
cons: Roman numerals take longer to read than Arabic numerals
A 24 inch dial can look modest on a very large wall

products.name: Westclox 20 Inch Traditional Large Wall Clock, Black with Gold Edge
products.description:
Westclox sells a 20 inch traditional clock with a black frame and gold-highlighted edges, a large dial and bold numerals. The brand is an established clockmaker, and the design suits living rooms, bedrooms and offices. At 20 inches it sits near the low end of the cost range.

A 20 inch clock is modest, so it works on smaller walls or in groupings, but it can look small on a large sofa wall. The tradeoff is that the gold edge is a more traditional look, which may not suit a modern room. Compared with the 24 inch CLXEAST, the Westclox is smaller and lighter and costs less, but it lacks the thick frame and the silent claim.

Hang it at eye level with a stud or an anchor. Insert a battery and set the time. If you are sensitive to ticking, put it in a living room rather than a bedroom, since the listing does not promise silence. Dust the frame with a dry cloth. It suits a traditional living room, a kitchen or a hallway where a classic dial is wanted at a modest cost.
products.bestFor: Smaller walls and traditional rooms that want a classic dial from a known brand.
pros: Bold numerals on a large dial are easy to read from across the room
A black frame with gold edges suits traditional decor
Low cost tier makes it easy to add to a gallery wall
A lighter weight is easy to hang on a standard hook
cons: A 20 inch diameter looks small on a large wall
The listing does not promise silent operation

products.name: SwallowLiving 24 Inch Vintage Iron Wall Clock, Silent, White Face
products.description:
SwallowLiving offers a 24 inch vintage iron clock with a white face, large bold black numbers, a silent quartz movement and a protective glass lens. The white face gives the strongest contrast of the group, so it is the easiest to read in a dim room. The retro look suits farmhouse and traditional spaces.

A glass lens adds weight and glare. The tradeoff is that glass can reflect a window or lamp and make the time harder to read at certain angles, and it is more fragile than a plastic lens. Compared with the CLXEAST, the SwallowLiving has a lighter, retro look and a white face, but a thinner frame.

Hang it where the glass will not reflect a bright window. Use a stud or a rated anchor, since a 24 inch iron and glass clock is heavier than a plastic one. Set the time and test the silent movement. Wipe the glass with a microfiber cloth and the frame with a dry cloth. It suits a kitchen, a dining room or a living room with a vintage or farmhouse style.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and dining rooms that want a high-contrast white face and a retro look.
pros: A white face with bold black numbers gives the best contrast
A silent quartz movement suits living areas
An iron frame with a glass lens feels solid and protected
A 24 inch diameter suits most feature walls
cons: Glass can reflect light and hide the time at some angles
Heavier than plastic-lens clocks and needs a solid anchor

products.name: Maxstar Large Round Wall Clock, Black Walnut Veneer with Black Metal Ring
products.description:
Maxstar combines a black walnut color wood veneer face with a thickened black iron outer ring and bold hollowed-out Arabic numerals. The movement is described as an upgraded silent mechanism that saves energy. The mix of wood and metal suits mid century and modern rooms, and the hollow numerals add texture.

Hollow numerals can be harder to read than solid ones on a busy background, since the wall shows through. The tradeoff is that a veneer face can show scratches and can warp in humid rooms. Compared with the CLXEAST, the Maxstar adds warmth with wood, but the face is less rugged than solid metal.

Hang the clock on a plain wall so the hollow numerals stand out. Use a stud or an anchor, set the time and test the silent sweep. Dust with a dry cloth, and avoid damp areas like a bathroom. A lighter wall behind the clock improves contrast. It suits a living room with wood furniture or a home office with a mid century look.
products.bestFor: Mid century and modern rooms that want warm wood with a black metal ring.
pros: A wood veneer face adds warmth next to black metal
Hollow Arabic numerals are bold and modern
An upgraded silent movement suits bedrooms and living rooms
A thickened iron ring gives structure to the frame
cons: Hollow numerals can blend into a busy wall
A veneer face is less rugged than solid metal

products.name: EMAX HOME 30 Inch Extra Large Farmhouse Wall Clock, Wood and Metal
products.description:
EMAX HOME makes a 30 inch farmhouse clock that blends real wood and metal with clear numerals and a silent non-ticking quartz movement. At 30 inches it becomes a focal point, big enough to anchor a blank wall over a sofa or a fireplace. The rustic wood and metal finish suits farmhouse and cottage rooms.

A 30 inch clock needs a stud or a heavy-duty anchor, and a wall with enough clear space around it. The tradeoff is cost and weight, since a large wood and metal clock is among the heavier ones in the group. Compared with the 24 inch SwallowLiving, the EMAX HOME is much larger and more rustic, but less versatile in small rooms.

Center it above a sofa or console with the bottom edge 6 to 8 inches above the furniture. Use a level, set the time and test the silent sweep. Dust the wood with a dry cloth, and avoid damp areas. Replace the battery yearly. It suits a large living room or a dining room where one oversized piece does the decorating for a bare wall.
products.bestFor: Large living rooms that need an oversized rustic clock as a focal point.
pros: A 30 inch diameter fills a large blank wall as a focal point
A wood and metal blend suits farmhouse and cottage rooms
A silent non-ticking movement is suited to living areas
Clear numerals read well from across the room
cons: Heavier and needs a stud or a heavy-duty anchor
A rustic style is less flexible for modern rooms

products.name: Vantic 32 Inch Oversized Wall Clock, Arabic Numerals, Wood and Metal
products.description:
Vantic makes a 32 inch oversized clock with large Arabic numerals in a wood and metal build that mixes vintage and modern styling. It is the largest clock in this group, and the oversized numerals read clearly at a distance. The listing notes that the hands should be set horizontal during shipping and handling to prevent the hour and minute hands from sticking together.

A 32 inch clock needs significant wall space and a strong anchor. The tradeoff is that it can dominate a small room, and the weight requires careful hanging. Compared with the EMAX HOME, the Vantic is two inches larger and more modern in its numerals, but they share a similar scale and cost.

Hang it where it has at least a foot of clear wall on each side. Use a stud or a heavy-duty anchor rated well above the weight. When you set the time, check that the hands do not touch, since the listing flags that issue. Dust with a dry cloth. It suits an open-plan living area, a high-ceiling room or a large entry where a standard clock would look lost.
products.bestFor: Open-plan rooms and high walls that need the largest clock in the group.
pros: A 32 inch diameter reads clearly across a large room
Oversized Arabic numerals are quick to read at a glance
A wood and metal build mixes vintage and modern styling
Large enough to fill a big wall with a single piece
cons: Needs a lot of wall space and a strong anchor
Hands can stick if they overlap, so check them after hanging

products.name: Zoirbly 16 Inch Glow-in-the-Dark Wall Clock with 3 Night Light Modes

specList.label: Light
specList.value: Glow face with 3 night light modes, including always on

products.description:
Zoirbly offers a 16 inch rustic clock with a glow face and three night light modes, including an always-on mode, designed so the time is visible in the dark and not just the glow. The movement is quiet, which suits bedrooms and living rooms. The lighting solves a common problem, because many lit clocks glow but do not show the time clearly.

A 16 inch clock is smaller than most of the group, so it is a bedroom or hallway clock, not a living room statement. The tradeoff is that the light modes may need batteries or power for the light, and always-on mode drains them faster. Compared with the CLXEAST, the Zoirbly is smaller and more functional, but less decorative.

Hang it in a bedroom, a hallway or a media room where you check the time at night. Choose the lighting mode that fits your routine, and replace the batteries when the glow dims. Dust the dial with a dry cloth, and avoid direct sunlight that can wear the glow face. It suits anyone who wakes at night and wants a readable dial without a bright screen.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and media rooms where the time must be readable in the dark.
pros: A glow face with three night modes keeps the time visible in the dark
A quiet movement suits bedrooms and living areas
A 16 inch diameter fits hallways and bedroom walls
A rustic design suits farmhouse and cabin rooms
cons: At 16 inches it is too small for a living room statement
Always-on mode uses battery power faster

buyingCriteria.explanation: A clock over furniture should be roughly one third to one half the furniture width. A 24 inch clock suits a 60 to 72 inch console, while a 30 inch EMAX HOME or a 32 inch Vantic suits a large sofa wall. Too small, like a 16 inch clock on an open wall, looks lost. Tape a paper circle on the wall to preview.

Bold Arabic numerals on a high-contrast face, as on the SwallowLiving, read fastest. Roman numerals, as on the CLXEAST, look classic but take longer to read. Hollow numerals, as on the Maxstar, depend on the wall behind them. Choose a style that everyone in the household can read.

Quartz movements are common, and silent sweep versions avoid the tick. Clocks like the CLXEAST and EMAX HOME list non-ticking movements. A loud tick is a nuisance in bedrooms. Check the product listing for a silent claim, and test it after hanging.

Metal, iron and wood frames give a premium feel but weigh more than plastic. A 30 inch wood and metal clock can weigh several pounds and needs a stud or a rated anchor. A thin frame can bend, and a thick frame, like the 0.8 inch CLXEAST, adds depth. Check the hanging hardware.

Glass lenses, as on the SwallowLiving, protect the dial but reflect light. Open dials, as on the Maxstar, avoid glare but collect dust. Place the clock away from direct window reflections. Matte finishes reduce glare.

A glow or lit dial, as on the Zoirbly, helps at night but adds batteries or power. Many clocks have no light at all. If you check the time in the dark, choose a lit clock or put a lamp nearby. A bright display can disturb sleep, so choose a dimmable one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and proportion
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared diameters from 16 to 32 inches and matched them to wall and furniture sizes. The CLXEAST 24 inch was judged a versatile size. The Vantic 32 inch was judged for large walls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Readability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at numeral style, face contrast and lens type. The SwallowLiving white face earned credit for contrast. Hollow numerals like the Maxstar were noted for wall dependence.

howWeEvaluated.title: Movement and noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked silent or non-ticking claims. The CLXEAST, EMAX HOME and SwallowLiving list silent movements. The Westclox does not promise silence.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared metal, iron, wood and veneer builds and the hanging hardware. The CLXEAST frame thickness was credited. Heavy clocks were judged on anchor needs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each clock in a cost tier from the cheapest Westclox to the EMAX HOME and Vantic. Tier is used for ordering only. Night light and extras were credited when useful.

maintenance.why: A weak battery makes a clock run slow or stop. A yearly swap avoids surprises.
Dust dulls numerals and builds on hollow faces. A dry cloth is enough.
A loose hook or anchor can let a heavy clock tilt or fall.
Hands can bend or touch. Adjust them if they drag or stick.
Sun fades finishes and warms the lens. Choose a shaded wall.

faq.q: How big should a wall clock be?
faq.a: Aim for about one third to one half the width of the furniture below. A 24 inch clock suits a 60 to 72 inch console. Preview with a paper circle.

faq.q: What is the best budget pick?
faq.a: The Westclox 20 inch is the lowest cost tier, and the CLXEAST 24 inch is the next step up with a silent movement.

faq.q: Do silent clocks really not tick?
faq.a: Silent sweep movements avoid the tick, but a faint sweep sound can remain. Test after hanging, and avoid placing the clock right above a bed if you are sensitive.

faq.q: How do I hang a heavy clock?
faq.a: Use a stud or a rated anchor, and make sure the hook is in good condition. Hang it at eye level with the center near 57 to 60 inches from the floor.

faq.q: How often do I replace the battery?
faq.a: Usually once a year with a single AA battery. Replace it sooner if the clock slows. Remove dead batteries to avoid leaks.

faq.q: Can I use a large clock in a bedroom?
faq.a: Yes, if it is silent and not too bright. A lit clock like the Zoirbly helps at night, but avoid bright displays that disturb sleep.
